title: Brush the debris off a boot sole
description: A rubber boot stands sole-up on a boot-rack peg in a collection tray with six dry soil clods lodged in its tread; pick up the shoe brush from the counter with the right hand of a Tianji Marvin two-arm robot (Sharpa Wave by default, or Wuji Hand 2.2), brush every clod off the sole into the tray and withdraw the brush; a clod outside the tray, a clod touched by the hand, a dropped brush, a displaced boot or any arm/stand contact fails the episode at once.
instruction: Brush all six soil clods off the upward-facing sole of the boot into the collection tray. The boot stands sole-up on a fixed boot-rack peg inside the tray (its sole plane is at z = 1.292 m); six small dry soil clods are lodged in its tread, held there by gravity and friction only (no glue or cohesive bond is simulated, so a clod moves as soon as something pushes it). The shoe brush lies bristles-down on the counter: pick it up with the robot's right hand and sweep the sole with the bristles. Success requires, in order: (1) the brush's bristle field touches the boot while the hand touches the brush and the brush does not touch the counter, for at least 10 controls in total; (2) every clod has been touched by the brush's bristle field (contact with the wooden back does not count) while it was still up on the boot (clod centre at most 0.01 m below the sole plane), and every clod centre lies inside the tray walls (x in [0.366, 0.694] m, y in [-0.184, 0.384] m) below the wall top (z < 0.931 m); (3) then, for 50 consecutive controls (1 s), all six clods stay in the tray with linear speed at most 0.05 m/s while the brush touches neither the boot nor any clod and is withdrawn (bristle-field centre at least 0.04 m above the sole plane, or at least 0.18 m horizontally from the sole centre). The episode ends with success at that moment; fewer than six clods never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the boot moves more than 0.03 m or tilts more than 0.35 rad from its reset pose; when a clod touches the counter or the floor, falls below the counter top (z < 0.886 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [0.25, 1.2] m, y in [-0.45, 0.45] m, z in [0.886, 1.8] m; when any part of the right hand touches a clod (clods must be brushed, not picked); when the brush touches the floor, the tray or the rack, falls below the counter top, leaves the workspace box, or is released in the air (it touches nothing but clods while its centre of mass sinks faster than 0.2 m/s); when any part of the robot other than its right hand (the stand, the torso, a link of either arm, the parked left hand) touches anything, including the robot itself; or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed: no welds, teleports, scripted object motion or applied object forces. The boot, brush and clods are free rigid bodies; the brush's 32 bristle tufts touch the world through one compliant bristle-pad contact proxy (individual fibre bending is not simulated) and the clods are rigid (no fracture or adhesion). The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.
mechanism: free boot on a fixed rack peg, free brush and six free clods; contact and gravity only
modeling: Rigid boot (Poly Haven Rubber Boots, CC0) with the source scene's 292 convex contact patches and an invisible interior proxy (footbed pad and shaft sleeve) that rests on the square rack peg; rigid 1 g clods with friction only (the source scene's cohesive bond law is not used); brush bristles as one compliant contact pad; rubber-lined tray floor with soft, well-damped contact.
